topics.displayName: Ask him what he saw or heard

lines.text: Mark is sitting against the wall of the gas station, shivering and muttering under his breath.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Noises. Last night, before, always. Banging down below. Like someone pounding to be heard and nobody hears.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: Banging from where?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: From the motel. Under the motel. There's people down there. Locked-up people. Told Frank once and he laughed.
He talks fast, jumps from one idea to the next, but there's a pattern underneath the rambling.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: I believe you, Mark. Go on.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yeah? Nobody ever believes me. Not even me, sometimes.
He calms down a little, looking me in the eye.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Hale. Always Hale going down there at night. With a bag, with a box. Never goes down empty-handed.

topics.displayName: Cut him off, he doesn't sound reliable

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: I get it, Mark. Thanks.
I don't believe him. And it shows right away.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Sure. Like everyone else. The crazy man talks, the crazy man doesn't matter.

topics.displayName: Ask him about that night again

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Empty bottles... it all blurs together. The cold, the wind. I don't know anything, I don't remember anything.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: What about those footsteps you kept hearing?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: What footsteps? Leave me alone. You already told me you don't believe me.
He turns to face the wall. There's no getting anything else out of him now.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Footsteps. Almost every night, footsteps going down.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: And the night the girl died?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: That one... no. That night's a blank. Like someone tore it right out of my head.
It's the first time I've seen him admit he doesn't know something, instead of making it up.
